## Introduction

`gmediation` is developed to conduct causal mediation/path analysis for
multiple mediators in two stages. The package provides two main functions:

- `gmediate()` estimates individual path effects, first- and second-stage
  mediator effects, and the total exposure effect, together with bootstrap
  confidence intervals.
- `gmedsens()` extends the same modeling framework with a probabilistic
  sensitivity analysis, re-evaluating path effects that are non-identifiable
  across a range of assumed correlations between mediator/outcome residuals,
  and reporting both tables and sensitivity plots.

Conceptually, both functions estimate the path effects from an exposure X to
a response Y through one or more first-stage mediators (e.g. `m11`, `m12`)
and one or more second-stage mediators (e.g. `m21`, `m22`, `m23`).

## Install and load the package

### Installing the package

Install directly from CRAN:

```r
install.packages("gmediation")
```

or, from a local source tarball:

```r
install.packages("gmediation_1.0.0.tar.gz", repos = NULL, type = "source")
```

### Loading the package

```{r setup}
library(gmediation)
```

## Example data

The examples in this vignette use the built-in `dental` data, which loads
automatically with the package (there is no need to call `data(dental)`
manually). There are 13 variables in the dataset, for 205 children.

```{r}
head(dental, 10)
```

| Variable | Type      | Definition                                                          |
| -------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ID       | character | permuted subject ID                                                   |
| dmft     | numeric   | count of decayed, missing, or filled teeth                            |
| SEX      | binary    | 1 if male; 0 if female                                                |
| grpbpd   | binary    | 1 if BPD (bronchopulmonary dysplasia); 0 otherwise                    |
| grpvlb   | binary    | 1 if VLBW (very low birth weight); 0 otherwise                        |
| brush    | binary    | 1 if brushes at least twice per day; 0 otherwise (1st-stage mediator) |
| visit    | binary    | 1 if taken to the dentist at most once per year; 0 otherwise (1st-stage mediator) |
| dmftd    | binary    | 1 if dmft is greater than 0; 0 if dmft equals 0 (outcome)             |
| seal     | binary    | 1 if has at least one dental sealant; 0 otherwise (2nd-stage mediator)|
| ses      | binary    | 1 if low socioeconomic status; 0 otherwise (exposure)                 |
| race     | binary    | 1 if African American; 0 otherwise                                    |
| ohi      | numeric   | Oral Hygiene Index, 0-3, higher is worse (2nd-stage mediator)         |
| momid    | character | permuted maternal ID; usable as a cluster variable                    |

## Reference group default

Both `gmediate()` and `gmedsens()` take a `ref` argument that defines the
empirical baseline covariate distribution used in the mediation formula. As
of this version, the default is `ref = "entire sample"`, meaning the whole
complete-case sample is used as the reference group unless a different
reference group is explicitly requested, e.g.
`ref = c("ses", c(0, 1))` to restrict to individuals with `ses` equal to 0
or 1. In the examples below we rely on this default.

## `gmediate()`: Example 1 (one mediator per stage)

In this example we conduct a mediation/path analysis explaining the effect
of `ses` on `dmftd` using one first-stage mediator (`brush`) and one
second-stage mediator (`seal`).

First, fit models for the response variable and each mediator. In this
example, `ses` is the exposure and `grpvlb`, `grpbpd`, `race`, `SEX` are
covariates. Because `dmftd`, `seal`, and `brush` are all binary, a logistic
model is used for each.

```{r}
model.y1 <- glm(dmftd ~ ses + grpvlb + grpbpd + race + SEX + brush + seal,
                 family = binomial, data = dental)
model.m11 <- glm(brush ~ ses + grpvlb + grpbpd + race + SEX,
                  family = binomial, data = dental)
model.m21 <- glm(seal ~ ses + grpvlb + grpbpd + race + SEX + brush,
                  family = binomial, data = dental)
```

The fitted models are then passed into `gmediate()`:

```{r}
single <- gmediate(data = dental, model.m1 = list(model.m11),
                    model.m2 = list(model.m21), model.y = model.y1,
                    expos = c("ses", 1), seed = 1234, boots = 100,
                    cluster = NULL, decomp = 1, CIPCT = 95,
                    xcorrv = c(0, 0.9), refmult = 1)
single
names(single)
```

Arguments used above:

- `data = dental` : `dental` is used as the original data
- `model.m1 = list(model.m11)` : the model fit for the first-stage mediator
- `model.m2 = list(model.m21)` : the model fit for the second-stage mediator
- `expos = c("ses", 1)` : `ses` is the exposure variable and `ses = 1` is
  the exposed group / `ses = 0` is the unexposed group
- `ref` : not specified, so the default `"entire sample"` is used
- `seed` : the seed used for bootstrap samples
- `boots` : number of bootstrap samples used for the confidence interval
- `cluster` : if the data has clusters, the cluster variable can be used to
  get cluster bootstrap samples (not used in this example, so standard
  bootstrap sampling of individuals is conducted)
- `decomp` : `gmediate` provides two choices of decomposition,
  characterized as an ordering to define path effects. Decomposition 1 is
  used here
- `CIPCT` : confidence level used for the bootstrap confidence interval
- `xcorrv` : sensitivity parameters used for non-identifiable paths
- `refmult` : the reference group multiplier; reference group samples are
  duplicated by this factor in the mediation formula computation to reduce
  Monte Carlo error

`names(single)` lists the objects returned by `gmediate()`: `indiv.path`,
`total.path`, `first.path`, `second.path`, `prop.indiv.path`,
`prop.first.path`, `prop.second.path`, `boot.est`, and `model.fit`. The
`*.path` objects give the estimated path effects, the `prop.*.path` objects
give the proportion of the total exposure effect mediated through each
path, `boot.est` gives the estimates from every bootstrap sample, and
`model.fit` gives the model fits from the complete-case data.

## `gmediate()`: Example 2 (two mediators per stage)

Here we explain the effect of `ses` on `dmftd` using two first-stage
mediators (`brush`, `visit`) and two second-stage mediators (`seal`,
`ohi`).

```{r}
model.y2 <- glm(dmftd ~ ses + grpvlb + grpbpd + race + SEX + brush + visit +
                   seal + ohi, family = binomial, data = dental)
model.m11 <- glm(brush ~ ses + grpvlb + grpbpd + race + SEX,
                  family = binomial, data = dental)
model.m12 <- glm(visit ~ ses + grpvlb + grpbpd + race + SEX,
                  family = binomial, data = dental)
model.m21 <- glm(seal ~ ses + grpvlb + grpbpd + race + SEX + brush + visit,
                  family = binomial, data = dental)
model.m22 <- glm(ohi ~ ses + grpvlb + grpbpd + race + SEX + brush + visit,
                  family = gaussian, data = dental)
```

```{r}
two_stage <- gmediate(data = dental, model.m1 = list(model.m11, model.m12),
                       model.m2 = list(model.m21, model.m22), model.y = model.y2,
                       expos = c("ses", 1), seed = 352, boots = 100,
                       cluster = NULL, decomp = 2, CIPCT = 95,
                       xcorrv = c(0, 0.9), refmult = 2)
two_stage
```

The meaning of the arguments is identical to Example 1. Here we call in two
first-stage and two second-stage mediators, use `seed = 352`, and use
decomposition option 2. The interpretation of the results is similar to
that of Example 1.

## `gmedsens()`: probabilistic sensitivity analysis

`gmedsens()` builds on the same model specifications used for `gmediate()`,
but evaluates how path effect estimates change across a grid of assumed
correlations (`xcorrv`) for paths that are not identifiable from the data
alone. This provides a way to assess how sensitive the substantive
conclusions are to that un-testable assumption. It also supports cluster
bootstrap resampling (via `cluster`), and can optionally write its summary
tables to CSV files (via `table_out`) and all of its sensitivity plots to a
single PDF file (via `plot_out`).

```{r, fig.show = "hold"}
gmedsens(data = dental, model.m1 = list(model.m11, model.m12),
         model.m2 = list(model.m21, model.m22), model.y = model.y2,
         expos = c("ses", 1), seed = 443095, boots = 100,
         cluster = "momid", decomp = 2, CIPCT = 95,
         xcorrv = c(0, 0.5, 0.9), scale = "MeanDiff",
         assumvars = c("dmftd", "ohi"), g = 1, ndig = 4,
         n_rows = 1, n_cols = 1, rows_per_page = 18, maxcnt = 100)
```

Arguments used above that are new relative to `gmediate()`:

- `cluster = "momid"` : `momid` identifies each child's mother; bootstrap
  resampling is performed by resampling mothers (clusters) with
  replacement, so that all children of a sampled mother are included together
- `xcorrv = c(0, 0.5, 0.9)` : the grid of assumed correlations evaluated for
  non-identifiable paths
- `assumvars = c("dmftd", "ohi")` : restricts the sensitivity evaluation to
  paths involving these variables
- `g` : a scaling factor applied to the assumed between-mediator /
  mediator-outcome correlation grid
- `ndig`, `n_rows`, `n_cols`, `rows_per_page` : control the formatting and
  pagination of the sensitivity tables/plots
- `table_out` : left at its default, `c("false", "")`, so no CSV files are
  written; set the first element to `"true"` and the second to a directory
  path to export the path-specific, first-stage, and second-stage
  sensitivity tables as CSV files
- `plot_out` : left at its default, `c("false", "")`, so no PDF is written;
  set the first element to `"true"` and the second to a directory path to
  save every sensitivity plot in one PDF file, `gmedsens_all_plots.pdf`

### Saving tables and plots

The example below writes the sensitivity tables and the plots PDF to a
temporary directory. In your own work, replace `tempdir()` with the folder
where you want the files to be saved (it is created if it does not exist).
When `assumvars = "ALL"` (the default), every pair of assumption variables is
evaluated; the exported CSV files then stack the results for all pairs, and
the `Rho.Between` column identifies the pair each row belongs to.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
out_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "gmedsens_output")
gmedsens(data = dental, model.m1 = list(model.m11, model.m12),
         model.m2 = list(model.m21, model.m22), model.y = model.y2,
         expos = c("ses", 1), seed = 443095, boots = 100,
         cluster = "momid", decomp = 2, CIPCT = 95,
         xcorrv = c(0, 0.5, 0.9), scale = "MeanDiff",
         plot_out = c("true", out_dir), table_out = c("true", out_dir))
list.files(out_dir)
```

`gmedsens()` is called primarily for its output (printed summary and
sensitivity tables/plots); see `?gmedsens` for full details of each
returned/printed component.

## See also

The [mediation](https://cran.r-project.org/package=mediation) package
provides related tools for causal mediation analysis with a single
mediator.
